newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds gave up some of their previous day's gains, chasing Bund futures to a lower close on Friday, but finished mainly higher on the week.
In thin trading, guilder paper performed in line with their German equivalents, which in turn were undermined by comments by a Bundesbank board member.
But a Reuters poll found that market players expected Dutch and German yields to continue converging over the next month.
A coincidental sharp drop on the Dutch sharemarket marred sentiment on the bond market if not actually prompting a move into fixed interest securities.
"I think the effect was probably psychological," said a dealer.
Dutch bonds opened slightly firmer, in line with the Bund contract, but they eased as the day proceeded.
The German market felt pressured particularly at the short end in response to comments to a German newspaper by Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum.
He was quoted as saying the central bank wanted to keep its options open in its weekly repo rate deliberations in view of the current uncertain environment.
This heightened fears of a German interest rate hike.
A Reuters poll of economists and dealers found they expected a continued rise in Dutch bond yields over the next month with yield spreads to Germany expected to continue shrinking.
Dutch yields have risen over the last month, with the short end worst hit, due to expectations of higher interest rates in Germany, which could feed through to the Netherlands.
U.S. Treasury bonds also opened lower in U.S. trading on a mix of profit taking and a weaker dollar.
Next week, the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday, Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday and French budget talks are expected to be the focus for financial markets.
